messages:
maria_support: FYI — Acme raised an escalated ticket. They see /v1/generate p99 jump from ~4.5s to ~12s starting ~2026-03-16T23:15Z. They attached screenshots. Customer is threatening a billing dispute. Can we triage? :eyes:

jasper_oncall: On it. Do we have any alerts fired? Which metric source did they query (customer dashboard vs our internal)?

observability_bot: Alert: high_p99_latency on service:inference-api - threshold 10s breached at 2026-03-16T23:18Z. Current p99 (ingest-rollup): 11.8s.

rachel_sre: I pulled the raw traces and spans for some sample requests. Backend token gen times look normal (~30-80ms). The long tail seems to be queueing on the model runtime layer — but only for regions in eu-west-1.

maria_support: Customer snapshot included their Grafana panel with p99 = 12.3s (they're using the panel's histogram quantile), while our public status board shows p99 = 5.1s. They claim we're hiding data.

jasper_oncall: Two hypotheses: 1) different metric derivations (rollup vs raw histogram quantiles), 2) different label filtering (maybe customer includes retries or edge proxy latencies). Can someone share the exact PromQL/aggregation we use for the public p99?

rachel_sre: Our public p99 uses rollup quantiles from aggregated histograms (rollup_quantile(0.99) over 5m windows) which can understate tails if bucket boundaries are coarse. Customer's panel does an instant quantile() on raw histograms ingested per-host, which can overestimate if there are fewer samples but high outliers. Also the customer's panel includes upstream proxy timings (x-forwarded) while our board excludes proxy by filter: service!~"edge-proxy".

jasper_oncall: Can you paste the queries? I want to reproduce both numbers locally.

rachel_sre: Sure — reproducer snippets below:

```
# Our public rollup (PromQL-like)
rollup_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

# Customer's instant quantile on raw histograms
quantile(0.99, rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="ingest-per-host"}[1m]))
```

rachel_sre: Also customer uses bucket boundaries up to 30s (we use 10s max), so anything >10s gets clamped into the last bucket and affects different derivations differently.

devin_product: So this is both an instrumentation mismatch (bucket boundaries) and a query mismatch. How urgent is mitigation vs educating the customer? They're billing-threat urgent per support.

jasper_oncall: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) enable cross-region fallback to a lower-latency model variant for eu-west-1 traffic temporarily, 2) increase burst capacity on Dedicated pools for that region, 3) surface an explainer to customer and share raw traces. What's fastest?

rachel_sre: Fastest -> change routing to use the smaller model variant for their tenantID via a routing rule (can be done in the next 10min). It lowers p99 but may slightly change output quality. Also I'll open a metrics fix: extend buckets to 60s for the ingest histograms and add a raw-quantile panel to our internal dashboard so we compare apples-to-apples.

maria_support: Customer approved temporary model fallback if we can commit to monitoring. They want an ETA and rollback plan.

jasper_oncall: I'll schedule the routing change now. @rachel_sre pls post the exact command once ready. I'll notify customer and set a 2-hour check-in.

rachel_sre: Command (internal routing CLI):

```
redwood-cli routing update --tenant acme-corp --route /v1/generate --model smaller-variant-v2 --priority temporary-esc
```

rachel_sre: Also adding the dashboard query so support can show side-by-side: 

```
# Raw per-host p99
quantile_over_time(0.99, http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="ingest-per-host"}[5m])

# Rollup p99 (what public board shows)
rollup_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

jasper_oncall: Deployed routing change at 2026-03-16T23:32Z. Observing client p99 drop from ~12s -> ~4.8s within two minutes. :thumbsup:

observability_bot: Metric update: service:inference-api eu-west-1 p99 = 4.9s (23:34Z).

maria_support: Customer confirmed noticeably better latency. They still want an explanation in writing and for us to fix dashboard mismatches.

devin_product: Next steps: 1) telemetry: align bucket boundaries across ingest and rollup (60s max), 2) dashboards: add both raw and rollup panels with a note about derivation method, 3) longer-term: consider exposing derivation type in the API so customers can choose. I'll file a PR for docs and tracking ticket.

rachel_sre: I'll open infra ticket to update histogram config and add a migration plan (risk: increased cardinality/storage for wider buckets). Recommend sampling policy adjustments too.

maria_support: Thanks all. I'll send the customer the mitigation timeline + screenshots showing before/after and include the explainer about bucket/derivation differences. Closing escalation if no further regressions. :white_check_mark:
